title: ENGL 103 or ENGL 104 (Introduction to Rhetoric and Composition)
description: A first-year writing course on academic reading, argument, research, and revision. Students write for different audiences and purposes.
notes: Choice slot: TAMU's ENGL 103 or ENGL 104. Official descriptions are in data/raw/tamu/ (courses-engl page).

title: University Core Curriculum
description: A general education course from the university's core curriculum, in an area such as creative arts, social and behavioral sciences, language and culture, American history, or government.
notes: TAMU: 21 core hours in the plan (see notes on the rows).

title: Science elective
description: A natural science course chosen from an approved list, such as biology, chemistry, geology, or further physics, often with a laboratory.
notes: TAMU: 7 hours from a list kept by advisors.

title: COMM 203 or COMM 205 or ENGL 210 (Public Speaking)
description: A communication course on presenting ideas to an audience, in speech or in writing for professional settings. Students practice organizing, supporting, and delivering information clearly.
notes: Choice slot: TAMU's COMM 203, COMM 205, or ENGL 210. Official descriptions are in data/raw/tamu/ (courses-comm and courses-engl pages).

title: Complementary elective
description: A course outside or alongside the major chosen with an advisor to support the student's goals, such as a minor, a certificate, or preparation for a career or graduate study.
notes: TAMU: 9 hours, approved on a filed degree plan.

title: MATH 251 or MATH 308 or STAT 212 (Engineering Mathematics III)
description: An additional mathematics or statistics course, such as multivariable calculus, differential equations, or a second statistics course.
notes: Choice slot: TAMU's MATH 251, MATH 308, or STAT 212. Official descriptions are in data/raw/tamu/ (courses-math and courses-stat pages).

title: Computer science elective
description: An upper-level computer science course chosen from the department's offerings, often organized into areas such as systems, software, and applications.
notes: TAMU: 18 hours spread over three areas plus upper-level electives.

title: High-Impact Experience
description: A required out-of-class learning experience, such as an internship, research, study abroad, or a service project, recorded on the transcript, usually for no credit.
